title: Texas-Sized Nuggets
statementMd:
Everything is bigger in Texas, so of course you want your chicken nuggets to be as big as it can be — but it still has to fit on your plate.

Your chicken nugget is described by 𝑛n points in the plane. The 𝑖i-th point is at integer coordinates (𝑥𝑖,𝑦𝑖)(xi,yi) with 0≤𝑥𝑖,𝑦𝑖≤1090≤xi,yi≤109.

You are given an integer scaling factor 𝑘k. Scaling the chicken nugget by 𝑘k moves every point (𝑥𝑖,𝑦𝑖)(xi,yi) to (𝑘⋅𝑥𝑖, 𝑘⋅𝑦𝑖)(k⋅xi, k⋅yi). You may **translate** the chicken nugget after it is scaled, but you may not rotate it.

The plate is an axis-aligned square whose corners are (0,0)(0,0) and (𝑚,𝑚)(m,m). The scaled chicken nugget fits on the plate if it is possible to translate it in such a way that every point lies inside the square or on its boundary.

Warning: you may need to use **64 bit integers** for this problem!

## Input

The first line contains three integers 𝑛n, 𝑚m, and 𝑘k (1≤𝑛≤2⋅1051≤n≤2⋅105; 1≤𝑚≤10181≤m≤1018; 1≤𝑘≤1091≤k≤109).

Each of the next 𝑛n lines contains two integers 𝑥𝑖xi and 𝑦𝑖yi (0≤𝑥𝑖,𝑦𝑖≤1090≤xi,yi≤109) — the coordinates of the 𝑖i-th point. Points are not necessarily distinct.

## Output

If the scaled chicken nuggy does not fit on the plate, print a single line containing `-1`.

Otherwise print the 𝑛n final points of the chicken nugget after scaling and possibly translating, one per line, each as two integers 𝑘⋅𝑥𝑖k⋅xi and 𝑘⋅𝑦𝑖k⋅yi. The points may be printed in any order.

## Note

In the first sample, 𝑘=2k=2, so the points scale to (10,10)(10,10), (12,14)(12,14), and (10,16)(10,16). As they stand they poke off the 10×1010×10 billboard, but the scaled logo is only 22 wide and 66 tall, so shifting it by (−10,−10)(−10,−10) places it at (0,0)(0,0), (2,4)(2,4), (0,6)(0,6) — entirely on the billboard.

In the second sample, 𝑘=3k=3 scales the logo to a 6×66×6 span, which is wider than the side length 55, so no translation can make it fit and the answer is `-1`.
